literal: Forgetfulness destroys fame, in the manner that daily poverty destroys wisdom.
translation: Just as constant poverty destroys one's wisdom, so does negligence destroy one's fame.
modern: தினசரி வறுமையானது ஒருவனுடைய அறிவை அழிப்பதைப் போல, மறதி அல்லது அலட்சியம் ஒருவனுடைய புகழை அழித்துவிடும்.
explanation: This couplet uses a powerful analogy to warn against negligence or forgetfulness (pocāppu). The poet compares the destructive power of negligence to that of constant, daily poverty (nicca nirappu). Just as relentless poverty wears down and ultimately destroys a person's wisdom and intellect (aṟivu), habitual carelessness or forgetfulness will ruin a person's hard-earned fame (pukaḻ). The word 'pocāppu' here denotes a state of mental slackness or lack of vigilance, which is shown to be fatal to one's reputation.
